DIST-002.summary: ct 23 October 2026 05:00Z ruling; target obligation retained with the missing implementation named in Status, no new DONE claim.
DIST-002.was: - **DIST-002 — Embed.** One asynchronous script or HTTPS iframe embeds the same respondent experience. It does not block the host page, and direct and embedded submissions produce the same response data and validation. Script embeds use an asynchronously loaded installation-origin script that mounts a sandboxed iframe without allow-same-origin, resizes to its content and emits only loaded, height and completed events. Exact allowed host origin, exact frame source, opaque child origin, challenge and field shape are checked. No answers, response identifiers, credentials or contact details enter the host URL, DOM or messages. The plain iframe option remains available.
DIST-002.now: - **DIST-002 — Embed.** One asynchronous script or HTTPS iframe embeds the same respondent experience. It does not block the host page, and direct and embedded submissions produce the same response data and validation. Script embeds use an asynchronously loaded installation-origin script that mounts a sandboxed iframe without allow-same-origin, resizes to its content and emits only loaded, height, completed and checkout events. Exact allowed host origin, exact frame source, opaque child origin, challenge and field shape are checked. No answers, response identifiers, credentials or contact details enter the host URL, DOM or messages. The plain iframe option remains available. The checkout message carries only the HTTPS Checkout URL on a Stripe-owned origin and the session ID, with no payer data. It is posted to the exact owner-configured embedding origin, never `*`; the host must be on the form's allowed-origin list or no checkout event is sent and the respondent gets the same-tab fallback. There is one handoff per payment attempt. No other new host event is permitted without ct's ruling.

RSLT-001.summary: ct 23 October 2026 05:00Z ruling; target obligation retained with the missing implementation named in Status, no new DONE claim.
RSLT-001.was: - **RSLT-001 — Response summary.** Every published revision has a results view that needs no `ai.provider.v1`: question answer summaries appear before session metrics. It shows completed responses, starts, completion rate, and average time to complete for the current filter, each beside the counts it was computed from. Imported completions remain in answer summaries and completed counts but are excluded from native starts, completion-rate numerators and duration samples, with the imported count stated separately. It is available from publication, shows zeros rather than an error before the first session, and never blocks on an analysis run. Answer summaries are never suppressed for operators who may read the form's responses and stay complete beside a suppressed RSLT-006 crosstab; in aggregate-only views RSLT-009's rule governs the crosstab, not the summaries.
RSLT-001.now: - **RSLT-001 — Response summary.** Every published revision has a results view that needs no `ai.provider.v1`: question answer summaries appear before session metrics. It shows completed responses, starts, completion rate, and average time to complete for the current combined filter bar (published-revision selector plus the response filters), each beside the counts it was computed from. Imported completions remain in answer summaries and completed counts but are excluded from native starts, completion-rate numerators and duration samples, with the imported count stated separately. It is available from publication, shows zeros rather than an error before the first session, and never blocks on an analysis run. Answer summaries are never suppressed for operators who may read the form's responses and stay complete beside a suppressed RSLT-006 crosstab; in aggregate-only views RSLT-009's rule governs the crosstab, not the summaries.

RSLT-003.summary: ct 23 October 2026 05:00Z ruling; target obligation retained with the missing implementation named in Status, no new DONE claim.
RSLT-003.was: - **RSLT-003 — Stated denominators.** Every percentage Pencil displays in results or analysis names the numerator and denominator it was computed from. A single-answer distribution divides by the responses that answered that question and its parts sum to that denominator. A multiple-choice distribution divides by the same denominator, may therefore total more than 100%, and is labeled as multiple-select. Completion rate divides native completed responses by native starts for the same revision and filter, excluding imported historical responses from both rate and duration calculations, and is never mixed with a per-question answer rate. Changing a filter changes both numerator and denominator together.
RSLT-003.now: - **RSLT-003 — Stated denominators.** Every percentage Pencil displays in results or analysis names the numerator and denominator it was computed from. A single-answer distribution divides by the responses that answered that question and its parts sum to that denominator. A multiple-choice distribution divides by the same denominator, may therefore total more than 100%, and is labeled as multiple-select. With a response-only filter active, completion shows started-to-completed among the filtered responses and states that view-based rates are unfiltered; with revision or date only, completion uses views. Imported historical responses are excluded from native starts, completion-rate numerators and duration calculations. Completion is never mixed with a per-question answer rate. Numerator and denominator always come from the same filtered set, which is named; changing a filter changes both together.

RSLT-004.summary: ct 23 October 2026 05:00Z ruling; target obligation retained with the missing implementation named in Status, no new DONE claim.
RSLT-004.was: - **RSLT-004 — Device split.** Results show the share of sessions in each RESP-013 device class, divided by the sessions counted for that revision and filter and named as RSLT-003 requires. Device class is derived at session start, is never stored on a response, and never appears in an export of responses.
RSLT-004.now: - **RSLT-004 — Device split.** Results show the device split following the combined filter bar (published-revision selector plus the response filters), with its numerator and denominator named as RSLT-003 requires. A coarse RESP-013 device class is derived at session start and stored on the response at start so it can be filtered: class only, no fingerprint, erased with the response. Revision-wide session counts without that response link do not satisfy the filtered split. Device class never appears in an export of responses.
